main_body: A bare, gnarled dead tree (trunk with forking branches and a few crows) with a flared root base
top_band: none (organic tree trunk and branches, no horizontal top surface; the column scan shows only dark brown trunk tones)
evidence: This is an organic tree: a vertical trunk with branches and a root flare, with no top slab or box volume. Rule 12 (caps) applies to columns and stelae, not trees. A tree seen as a trunk plus branches is the normal way to draw this subject in the 3/4 view, and no horizontal surface is expected on it. It does not break the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 11 distinct colours and a median of 7 colours per tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. The dark edge pixels are 93% neutral, so the outline is a near-black line rather than a tinted material tone. The trunk uses about 4 brown steps with little bark grain or per-clump highlighting, and the large dark bands read as flat. The references have rich multi-green clumps and tinted outlines, so next to them this tree looks thinner and more sticker-like.
